example.title: Six Penny Bridge, School Street (Old Schuylkill Road) over Sixpenny Creek

brief: Single-span reinforced-concrete closed-spandrel deck arch in a small village, 1907: about 66 ft long and 20 ft wide with a 32 ft clear span and 17 ft roadway, a low smooth barrel springing about 1 ft above ground and rising 6.5 ft. Incised outline of the arch ring, a 9-inch corbelled belt course along each face, 3.5 ft recessed-panel solid concrete parapets, and curved wing walls. An inscribed stone set in the parapet names the bridge, the year, the county commissioners, engineer, inspector and contractor.

traits.railing_detail: solid recessed-panel concrete parapet 3.5 ft high

names.plate: inscribed stone: SCHOOL STREET BRIDGE · BUILT 1907 · J. M. YODER, J. F. FIELDS, COUNTY COMMISSIONERS · C. B. CARVER, ENGINEER · HARTMAN & REESE, CONTRACTORS
